title: Canonical-byte polynomial arithmetic for cyclic_decomposition chain_polys
description:
Replace the scalar Montgomery polynomial-bookkeeping inside `cyclic_decomposition`'s `chain_polys` updates with canonical-byte polynomial arithmetic for `Fp

` with `P ≤ 251`, removing the ~16M Montgomery REDC operations that dominate `GF(251)/n=256` charpoly. ## Background `d1dd266c` landed `PackedFpMatrix

` + `PackedFpBasis

` so the matvec and basis-reduce arms of `cyclic_decomposition` run in canonical-byte form. The remaining hot path is the polynomial-bookkeeping loop that updates `chain_polys[k]` after each Krylov step — each update is `O(k)` field operations × `O(k)` substitutions, totalling `O(n^3)` Montgomery muls at `n=256`. Empirically: ~16M Mont muls × ~10 ns ≈ 160 ms estimated; measured 12.6 ms (zero-coefficient skips help). fflas runs the equivalent in 1.3 ms. ## Hard ceilings (fflas-ffpack reference) | Cell | fflas wall | 1.5x ceiling | Pre-task gf2 wall | Pre-task ratio | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | GF(251)/n=256 charpoly | 1.317 ms | 1.975 ms | 12.61 ms | 9.58x FAIL | ## Success Criteria - [hard] `GF(251)/n=256` charpoly meets the 1.5x ceiling (≤ 1.975 ms) on the current Zen 3 host, **OR is covered by a user-approved scope amendment to the broader 97bf0879 epic per the 2026-05-07 amendment below.** - [hard] `cyclic_decomposition`'s `chain_polys` updates execute in canonical-byte arithmetic for `Fp

` with `P ≤ 251`, with no Montgomery REDC inside the inner update loop. Scalar Montgomery path is retained as a fallback for non-`Fp` fields and for `P > 251`. - [hard] No regression on any other charpoly or minpoly cell currently PASSing. - [hard] Correctness: existing `cyclic_decomposition` invariants continue to pass; add a proptest comparing the canonical-byte chain_polys output to the scalar Montgomery output across random matrices over `Fp<7>` and `Fp<251>`, sizes n ∈ {2..32}. - [hard] Final evidence updates `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` (or a successor doc) with the new GF(251)/n=256 charpoly Criterion median + before/after comparison. ## Amendment — 2026-05-07 (user-approved) Per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-07: 5a3dbd5b delivered a 3x speedup (12.61 ms → 4.19 ms; 9.58x → 3.18x of fflas), but the residual gap to the 1.5x ceiling is below the granularity that further canonical-byte trait-level tuning can close. The remaining gap is the per-call AVX2 byte-lane operation overhead in `chain_polys`'s inner update loop; closing it requires hand-written register-scheduled kernels (architectural sibling to `70766cb1`'s panel-kernel inline work, but for the chain_polys surface). That work is filed as **`52cce970`** (Bespoke small-prime AVX2 kernel for GF(251) charpoly+minpoly residual cells) and tracked under the broader finite-field LA SOTA catch-up planning issue **`615db3b9`**, NOT as a blocker on this issue. Empirical basis: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` § 3.2, § 6.2. Re-escalation threshold: re-evaluate the GF(251)/n=256 charpoly cell when `52cce970` closes. ## Notes The replacement should ideally also speed up `GF(7)/n=256` charpoly (currently 0.82x — already PASSing, but the same algorithmic path benefits). No regression target on that cell; just measure post-implementation.

documents.label: Integrated post-sibling scorecard (chain_polys 3x speedup, residual tracked under 52cce970)
